+title: 'ACPC-4: ClientModelExtension, the session part (state on each SessionModel, `_` session updates)'
+---
+## What
+ACPC-4, the second part. An extension adds observable state to each `SessionModel`, and handles the `_` session updates that it knows.
+
+Today `SessionModel.engineChange(folding:)` (`Sources/FoundationModelsACPClient/Model/SessionModel.swift`, about line 554) has two hard-coded branches: `_mcp_server_status` (`MCPServerStatusUpdate`) and `_mail_delivery_paused` (`MailDeliveryPause`). Each other `_` update goes to the engine and becomes an `UnknownEntry`.
+
+Make these changes:
+- [ ] `Model/ClientModelExtension.swift`: add to the protocol
+  - `associatedtype SessionState: AnyObject & Observable` (with the same empty default as the connection state), and `func makeSessionState(for sessionId: SessionId) -> SessionState`.
+  - `func apply(_ update: SessionUpdate, to state: SessionState, connection: ConnectionState) -> Bool`. It gives `true` when the extension took the update. A taken update does not go to the engine and adds no transcript entry. Default: `false`.
+  - `func didStartSession(state: SessionState, request: ...)`: a hook for `session/new` and `session/resume`, so an extension can seed its state from the request (the MCP servers need this). Default: do nothing.
+- [ ] `Model/SessionModel.swift`: each `SessionModel` that the `ConnectionModel` makes gets one state for each registered extension. `public func extensionState<E: ClientModelExtension>(_ type: E.Type) -> E.SessionState?`. In `engineChange(folding:)`, give each `_` update (an unknown update kind) to the extensions in registration order before the built-in branches and the engine. The first extension that gives `true` takes it.
+- [ ] A chunk flush: an update that an extension takes must flush the chunk buffer first, as each other update does, so the applied order is the arrival order.
+- [ ] `ClientModelExtensionContext`: an extension notification handler can find the `SessionModel` of a `sessionId` and its extension state, for a session notification that is not a `session/update`.
+- [ ] Preview models (`Preview/SessionModel+Preview.swift`) can set an extension state with sample data.
+- [ ] DocC: add the session part to the extension article.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A test extension that takes `_test_status` updates changes its session state, and the transcript gets no entry.
+- [ ] An `_` update that no extension takes becomes an `UnknownEntry`, as today.
+- [ ] Two extensions: the first in registration order that gives `true` takes the update; the second does not see it.
+- [ ] Each session (also a sub-agent session and a resumed session) has its own state.
+- [ ] Chunks before and after a taken update keep arrival order.
+- [ ] `SessionModelMCPServerStatusTests` and `SessionModelMailPauseTests` stay green.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Extend `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/Model/ClientModelExtensionTests.swift` with the session cases above. Use `SessionUpdateFixtures.swift` and `CoalescingTestSupport.swift` for the chunk order case.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter "ClientModelExtensionTests|SessionModelMCPServerStatusTests|SessionModelMailPauseTests"` → all pass. Then `swift test` → all pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #step1
\ No newline at end of file
